title: Recursive CTE — Employee Hierarchy
description: Build an employee reporting chain using a recursive CTE.

data.text: Write a query that displays the employee reporting hierarchy from CEO down to each individual contributor.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
WITH EmployeeCTE AS (
    -- Anchor: CEO (no manager)
    SELECT
        EmployeeID,
        FirstName + ' ' + LastName AS EmployeeName,
        ManagerID,
        1 AS Level,
        CAST(FirstName + ' ' + LastName AS VARCHAR(MAX)) AS Path
    FROM Employees
    WHERE ManagerID IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive: employees with managers
    SELECT
        e.EmployeeID,
        e.FirstName + ' ' + e.LastName,
        e.ManagerID,
        ec.Level + 1,
        ec.Path + ' > ' + e.FirstName + ' ' + e.LastName
    FROM Employees e
    INNER JOIN EmployeeCTE ec ON e.ManagerID = ec.EmployeeID
)
SELECT EmployeeID, EmployeeName, ManagerID, Level, Path
FROM EmployeeCTE
ORDER BY Level, EmployeeName
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 100);

data.title: Explanation
data.text: Recursive CTEs have an anchor member (base case) and a recursive member that references the CTE itself. Always include OPTION (MAXRECURSION n) to prevent infinite loops from cycles in the data. The default limit is 100 iterations.
